notes.title: A bid is small
notes.science: A bid is any small reach for attention: a look, a wave, a sigh. In Gottman's lab, couples who stayed together turned toward each other's bids far more often than couples who split.
notes.limits: Those figures come from watching couples, so they show a link and not a cause. Pim is a few rules, not a partner.
notes.counter: Bids between strangers, or between a creature and its sky, may follow other rules.
notes.question: Did you notice Pim's first look before you did anything?

sources.label: Simply Psychology on the limits of the bid research

notes.title: Seeing a mind
notes.science: People read motion as a mind very fast. In a 1944 film, two triangles and a circle moved about, and nearly everyone who watched it told a story about a bully.
notes.limits: Pim looks up because a rule tells it to. The game borrows your habit of seeing a mind there.
notes.counter: Seeing a mind where there is none can also mislead us about storms, machines, and luck.
notes.question: What told you that Pim was alive?
